title: Hepatitis C: Screening and Referral for Treatment

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult in primary care, an emergency department or a liver clinic in Saudi Arabia who needs hepatitis C screening, confirmation of active infection, fibrosis assessment, referral or treatment with a direct-acting antiviral, on-treatment safety checks, cure confirmation and follow-up, using the Saudi Association for the Study of Liver diseases and Transplantation (SASLT) 2024 update, with US prescribing information for dilution-free administration details of each medicine.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi Ministry of Health hepatitis C protocol document was opened; the Saudi source is the SASLT 2024 update, which describes the Ministry of Health national screening and test-and-treat programme, so the authority is shown as Other.

Choice of the preferred regimen in each branch follows the order of the SASLT 2024 recommendations (sofosbuvir/velpatasvir listed first), because the guideline does not name a single preferred drug; confirm with the local liver service.

SASLT 2024 gives 8-week treatment of recently acquired infection (Grade B1) with any of three regimens; the US labels do not list 8 weeks for these drugs in acute infection, so this is shown from SASLT only.
Sofosbuvir plus daclatasvir has no US prescribing information in the sources opened (daclatasvir is not marketed in the US); its doses and interaction rules are from SASLT 2024 only.

The interaction table in SASLT 2024 (Table 1) lost some column alignment in text extraction, so only rows whose four columns are unambiguous are quoted; the full list must be checked on the Liverpool hepatitis drug interaction website for each patient.

Ribavirin dosing with direct-acting antivirals (1,000 mg or 1,200 mg a day by weight; 600 mg start in decompensated cirrhosis) is from SASLT 2024 and the EPCLUSA label; renal and haemoglobin adjustment is from the ribavirin tablet label, which is written for use with peginterferon.
Figures were read through automated extraction of the open-access journal XML and the DailyMed label XML; spot-check each dose against the source during clinical review.
Paediatric dosing, genotype-specific resistance testing methods, and liver transplant protocols are outside the scope of this adult primary-care and referral topic and are only mentioned briefly.

The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration was not checked there. Registration of sofosbuvir (Sovira, Sofocure), daclatasvir (Levera), sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (Epclusa), sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir (Vosevi) and glecaprevir/pibrentasvir (Maviret) is taken from SASLT 2024 Table 2; ribavirin registration is not verified.

pathophysiology.summary: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is a blood-borne ribonucleic acid (RNA) virus. Saudi Arabia has a low prevalence (antibody 0.23% and active infection about 0.1%), and 61% of antibody-positive people are older than 40 years, so screening is built around finding long-standing infection (SASLT 2024, Section Epidemiology). Control rests on a safe blood supply, strict infection control in healthcare and few people who inject drugs; case finding uses the national screening programme, premarital screening and test-and-treat in primary care (SASLT 2024, Section Epidemiology). Antibody tests show exposure only. Active infection needs HCV RNA (or HCV core antigen) detected; people who cleared the virus or were cured keep antibodies and are not protected from reinfection (SASLT 2024, Sections Diagnosis and Post-treatment follow-up). Direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) block viral proteins NS5A, NS5B (sofosbuvir) and NS3/4A (glecaprevir, voxilaprevir). The aim is sustained virological response 12 weeks after treatment (SVR12), meaning HCV RNA at or below 15 IU/mL, which is a cure in virtually all patients (SASLT 2024, Section Primary goal). Cure lowers liver complications but does not remove the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in advanced fibrosis (F3) or cirrhosis, so surveillance continues after cure (SASLT 2024, Section Primary goal). Protease inhibitors reach much higher blood levels in decompensated cirrhosis and can cause liver injury, and suppressing HCV can reactivate hepatitis B virus (HBV); both drive the pre-treatment checks (SASLT 2024, Sections Contraindications and HBV and HIV testing).

symptoms: Most people have no symptoms; infection is found by screening in primary care, premarital screening, blood donation, dialysis units or raised liver enzymes (SASLT 2024, Section Screening and treatment strategy).
Late disease: jaundice, vomiting blood, confusion, abdominal swelling and leg swelling (SASLT 2024, Table 3).
Outside the liver: cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis, HCV-related kidney disease and HCV-related malignancy (SASLT 2024, Section Indications for therapy).
physicalSigns: Cirrhosis or decompensation: jaundice, ascites, leg oedema, nodular liver or splenomegaly on imaging, platelets below 150,000/mm3 (SASLT 2024, Table 3 and Table 7).
Skin, joint or kidney signs of cryoglobulinaemia.
redFlags: Jaundice, vomiting blood, confusion, ascites or leg oedema (decompensated cirrhosis, CTP class B or C): refer to a liver unit, ideally a transplant centre; never use a protease-inhibitor regimen (glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir) (SASLT 2024, Section Decompensated cirrhosis).
HBsAg positive or anti-HBc positive: HBV may reactivate during or after DAA therapy; send HBV DNA and start HBV prophylaxis before DAAs if HBsAg positive (SASLT 2024, Section HBV coinfection).
Pregnancy, or a woman planning pregnancy: do not start a DAA course during pregnancy; ribavirin is teratogenic (SASLT 2024, Section Safety of DAAs; ribavirin label, Section 4).
Patient on amiodarone: sofosbuvir-containing regimens can cause symptomatic bradycardia; do not combine (SASLT 2024, Section Drug-drug interactions).
Patient on rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital or St. John's wort: all DAAs fail; stop or substitute the interacting drug first (SASLT 2024, Table 1).
During treatment: ALT 10 times above baseline, or any ALT rise with jaundice or hepatitis symptoms: stop the DAA and refer (SASLT 2024, Section Protease inhibitor liver injury).
Liver mass or rising alpha-fetoprotein in cirrhosis: urgent hepatology referral for HCC (SASLT 2024, Section HCC).
precipitants: Contaminated blood, injections or healthcare procedures; injection drug use (SASLT 2024, Section Epidemiology).
Dialysis; HIV or HBV coinfection (SASLT 2024, Sections Renal impairment and HIV).
Alcohol, diabetes, obesity and steatotic liver disease speed fibrosis (SASLT 2024, Section HBV and HIV testing).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Anti-HCV positive but HCV RNA not detected; repeat RNA at 12 and 24 weeks if recent exposure is suspected (SASLT 2024, Recommendations, Section Recently acquired HCV).
Within 6 months of exposure; antibody may be negative early, so test HCV RNA (SASLT 2024, Section Diagnosis and Section Recently acquired HCV).
Test HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs and HIV in everyone; HBV DNA can be low or undetectable while HCV is active (SASLT 2024, Section HBV and HIV testing).

differentials.condition: Other liver disease (alcohol, steatotic liver disease, autoimmune)
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Persisting abnormal liver tests after cure; check iron studies, autoantibodies, coeliac serology, copper, ceruloplasmin, alpha-1-antitrypsin, glucose and lipids (SASLT 2024, Table 5).
Rapid test positive with negative reflex RNA and a negative repeat; confirm with a laboratory enzyme immunoassay (SASLT 2024, Section Diagnosis).

ruleIn.testName: Anti-HCV antibody (rapid point-of-care test or laboratory enzyme immunoassay)

clinicalManagement.title: Test and confirm active infection
actions: Offer anti-HCV to every adult not yet tested, including at routine primary-care visits (Check and Reassure programme), premarital screening and in all high-risk groups (SASLT 2024, Section Screening and treatment strategy).
Use a laboratory enzyme immunoassay or a rapid finger-prick test; a positive result needs HCV RNA (or core antigen) from the same visit by reflex testing (SASLT 2024, Section Diagnosis, Grade A1).
Antibody positive and RNA not detected: the patient is not infected now; if exposure was within 6 months repeat RNA at 12 and 24 weeks (SASLT 2024, Section Recently acquired HCV).
Antibody negative with unexplained hepatitis, or immunosuppressed: send HCV RNA directly (SASLT 2024, Section Diagnosis).

clinicalManagement.title: Decide who treats the patient
actions: Primary-care treatment (simplified pathway): treatment-naive, any genotype, no cirrhosis or compensated cirrhosis (CTP A) (SASLT 2024, Table 7).

Refer to a hepatologist, gastroenterologist or infectious diseases specialist: cirrhosis, renal impairment or dialysis, multiple co-morbidities, previous treatment, HBV or HIV coinfection, post-transplant, pregnancy, or any sign of decompensation (SASLT 2024, Section Screening and treatment strategy).
Refer to a liver transplant centre: CTP class B or C cirrhosis (SASLT 2024, Section Decompensated cirrhosis, Grade C1).
Do not delay treatment while waiting for fibrosis tests if the patient may be lost to follow-up (SASLT 2024, Section Pre-treatment fibrosis assessment).

clinicalManagement.title: Pre-treatment checklist
actions: Record prior HCV treatment, symptoms of decompensation, alcohol, diabetes, vaccination history and every medicine, herbal product and supplement (SASLT 2024, Table 3).
Send full blood count, ALT, AST, albumin, bilirubin, eGFR, quantitative HCV RNA, HIV, HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs and anti-hepatitis A virus IgG; add INR in cirrhosis (SASLT 2024, Table 3).
Stage fibrosis with FIB-4 or elastography; liver ultrasound within 3 months if cirrhosis (SASLT 2024, Table 3).

Serum pregnancy test in women of childbearing age; advise against pregnancy until the course is done; two reliable contraceptive methods during and 6 months after ribavirin (SASLT 2024, Section Safety of DAAs).

HBsAg positive: send HBV DNA, assess against the SASLT HBV treatment criteria, and give HBV nucleos(t)ide prophylaxis that continues until 12 weeks after the DAA course (SASLT 2024, Section HBV coinfection, Grade B1).
Check interactions on the Liverpool hepatitis drug interaction site; stop or switch amiodarone, enzyme-inducing antiepileptics, rifamycins, St. John's wort and bosentan (SASLT 2024, Table 1).
Warn patients with diabetes that glucose may fall as the virus clears; adjust diabetes medicines (SASLT 2024, Section HBV and HIV testing, Grade C1).

clinicalManagement.title: Start a pangenotypic DAA
clinicalManagement.timeframe: As soon as RNA is confirmed
actions: No cirrhosis, treatment-naive: sofosbuvir/velpatasvir 12 weeks, or glecaprevir/pibrentasvir 8 weeks, or sofosbuvir plus daclatasvir 12 weeks, whatever the genotype (SASLT 2024, Table 8).

Compensated cirrhosis: sofosbuvir/velpatasvir 12 weeks (genotype 3 only without the NS5A resistance substitution Y93H, otherwise add ribavirin); glecaprevir/pibrentasvir 8 weeks; sofosbuvir plus daclatasvir with ribavirin for 12 weeks or 24 weeks without ribavirin (SASLT 2024, Table 9).
Decompensated cirrhosis (specialist only): sofosbuvir/velpatasvir or sofosbuvir plus daclatasvir with ribavirin 12 weeks, or 24 weeks without ribavirin; no protease inhibitors (SASLT 2024, Table 10).
Severe renal impairment or dialysis: glecaprevir/pibrentasvir once daily with food (SASLT 2024, Section Renal impairment, Grade B1).

Recently acquired infection: 8 weeks of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir or sofosbuvir plus daclatasvir (SASLT 2024, Section Recently acquired HCV, Grade B1); no post-exposure treatment without documented transmission.
Generic drugs may be used if quality is assured by the provider (SASLT 2024, Recommendations, Grade A1).
Give written advice on dose, food, missed doses, side effects and not starting new medicines without asking (SASLT 2024, Section Monitoring, Grade D1).

clinicalManagement.title: On treatment
actions: Most patients need no tests during treatment; arrange a review for adherence, side effects and interactions; common side effects are headache, nausea, diarrhoea and fatigue (SASLT 2024, Section Monitoring).
Added ribavirin: check haemoglobin more often; reduce ribavirin as the label states (Hb below 10 g/dL) (SASLT 2024, Section Monitoring; ribavirin label, Section 2.3).

Stop the DAA if ALT is 10 times above baseline, or if ALT rises less than that with jaundice, weakness, nausea, vomiting or raised bilirubin, ALP or INR (SASLT 2024, Section Protease inhibitor liver injury, Grade B1).

Missed doses in the first 4 weeks: 7 days or less, resume and finish; 8 days or more, resume at once and send HCV RNA the same day; RNA detected above 25 IU/mL, extend by 4 weeks (SASLT 2024, Table 6).
Missed doses after week 4: 7 days or less, resume; 8 to 20 days, resume and send RNA, stop and retreat if detected; 21 days or more, stop and send RNA (SASLT 2024, Table 6).
Warfarin: check INR during and after treatment; antiretroviral and calcineurin-inhibitor interactions need specialist review (SASLT 2024, Section Drug-drug interactions).

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm cure and follow up
clinicalManagement.timeframe: 12 weeks after the last dose and after
actions: Send HCV RNA and liver tests 12 weeks after the last dose (SVR12); SVR4 can be used if the patient may not return (SASLT 2024, Table 5 and Section Post-SVR follow-up).
SVR12 reached, not F3 or cirrhosis, liver tests normal: no further HCV clinic follow-up; explain that antibodies remain and do not give immunity (SASLT 2024, Table 5, Grade B1).
SVR12 reached with abnormal liver tests: look for other liver disease and refer to a hepatologist if managed in primary care (SASLT 2024, Table 5).
F3 or cirrhosis: ultrasound every 6 months with or without alpha-fetoprotein, for life, plus non-invasive portal hypertension checks (SASLT 2024, Section Post-SVR follow-up, Grade B1 and D1).
Ongoing risk of reinfection: HCV RNA yearly (SASLT 2024, Recommendations, Grade D1).

Untreated or failed patients: liver tests, full blood count and INR every 6 to 12 months and ultrasound every 6 months if advanced fibrosis (SASLT 2024, Section Follow-up of untreated patients, Grade C1).
Vaccinate non-immune patients against hepatitis A and hepatitis B after DAAs are complete (SASLT 2024, Section HBV and HIV testing).

clinicalManagement.title: Treatment failure and special groups
actions: Failure after a DAA with a protease or NS5A inhibitor: sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir 12 weeks (add weight-based ribavirin in genotype 3 with compensated cirrhosis), or glecaprevir/pibrentasvir 16 weeks (not after both NS3/4A and NS5A exposure, and not in genotype 3 with prior sofosbuvir/NS5A) (SASLT 2024, Section Retreatment, Grade A1).

Failure after glecaprevir/pibrentasvir: glecaprevir/pibrentasvir plus sofosbuvir plus ribavirin 16 weeks, or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir 12 weeks (Grade B2); multiple failures: glecaprevir/pibrentasvir plus sofosbuvir plus ribavirin 16 weeks, or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir 24 weeks (Grade B2).
HIV coinfection: same regimens as monoinfection with careful antiretroviral interaction review (SASLT 2024, Section HIV, Grade B1).

Liver transplant recipients: treat as soon as stable, within the first month if possible; sofosbuvir/velpatasvir or glecaprevir/pibrentasvir for 12 weeks (SASLT 2024, Section Liver transplant, Grade B1).
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) eligible for resection or ablation: delay DAAs until HCC treatment is finished (SASLT 2024, Section HCC, Grade A1).

Pregnancy: no DAA has an approved pregnancy indication; couples with HCV should be treated before marriage; breastfeeding is allowed unless the nipples are cracked or bleeding (SASLT 2024, Section Pregnancy).

regimens.indication: Chronic HCV, any genotype, treatment-naive, no cirrhosis
regimens.patientGroup: Adults with chronic HCV without cirrhosis
regimens.dose: One fixed-dose tablet of sofosbuvir 400 mg plus velpatasvir 100 mg. Dilution and preparation: none; oral film-coated tablet, no crushing or reconstitution.
regimens.route: Oral; swallow the tablet whole once daily at the same time each day, with or without food (Epclusa label, Section 2.3)
adjustments: Renal: no dose change at any eGFR including dialysis (EPCLUSA label, Section 2.5).
Hepatic: no dose change in CTP A, B or C (EPCLUSA label, Section 8.7).

Pregnancy and breastfeeding: safety of direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) is not established; women of childbearing age are advised to avoid pregnancy and breastfeeding during treatment and to wait until the course is complete (SASLT 2024, Section Safety of DAAs).

Acid suppression: with velpatasvir give no more than omeprazole 20 mg once daily (or equivalent: lansoprazole 30 mg, esomeprazole 20 mg, pantoprazole 40 mg, rabeprazole 20 mg) or famotidine 20 mg twice daily; separate aluminium/magnesium antacids by 4 hours (SASLT 2024, Table 4).
Check every co-medication on the University of Liverpool hepatitis drug interaction checker before the first dose (SASLT 2024, Section Drug-drug interactions).
SFDA: registered in Saudi Arabia as Epclusa 400 mg/100 mg (SASLT 2024, Table 2).
monitoring: Quantitative HCV RNA 12 weeks after the last dose (SVR12); liver tests at the same visit; no routine on-treatment HCV RNA unless adherence is a concern (SASLT 2024, Table 5).

medicationPlan.note: Regimens follow SASLT 2024 Tables 2, 8, 9 and 10 and its Recommendations; administration, contraindications and renal or hepatic rules were checked against the US prescribing information for Epclusa, Mavyret, Vosevi and ribavirin. diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Everyone at least once; mass screening since 2018, expanded to all ages; plus premarital, dialysis, blood donor, people who inject drugs, prisons and selected hospital screening (SASLT 2024, Section Screening and treatment strategy).

Anti-HCV positive by enzyme immunoassay or rapid test AND HCV RNA detected (lower limit of detection 15 IU/mL or less) or HCV core antigen detected; do reflex RNA on the same sample (SASLT 2024, Section Diagnosis, Grade A1).
Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) score above 3.25, or transient elastography above 12.5 kPa, or platelets below 150,000/mm3, or nodular liver or splenomegaly, or biopsy-proven cirrhosis (SASLT 2024, Table 7).
Treatment-naive, any genotype, no cirrhosis or compensated cirrhosis (CTP A) (SASLT 2024, Table 7).
Cirrhosis, renal impairment, multiple co-morbidities, post-liver transplant, prior DAA failure, HBV or HIV coinfection, decompensation (SASLT 2024, Section Screening and treatment strategy).
Fibrosis stage 2 or more, cirrhosis, HIV or HBV coinfection, transplant, extrahepatic complications, women who plan pregnancy, premarital positive (SASLT 2024, Section Indications for therapy).
HCV RNA 15 IU/mL or less 12 or more weeks after the last dose (SASLT 2024, Section Primary goal, Grade A1).

teaching.scope: Adult in primary care, an emergency department or a liver clinic in Saudi Arabia who needs hepatitis C screening, confirmation of active infection, fibrosis assessment, referral or treatment with a direct-acting antiviral, on-treatment safety checks, cure confirmation and follow-up, using the Saudi Association for the Study of Liver diseases and Transplantation (SASLT) 2024 update, with US prescribing information for dilution-free administration details of each medicine.
learningObjectives: Confirm active HCV with antibody and reflex RNA, and decide who treats the patient.
Choose the correct pangenotypic regimen and duration for the branch the patient is in.
Know the contraindications, interactions and stop rules before the first dose.
Confirm cure at 12 weeks and continue liver cancer surveillance when fibrosis is advanced.
pitfalls: Treating a positive antibody without sending RNA.
Starting a DAA without checking HBV status and co-medications.
Using ribavirin in pregnancy or in a patient with an unstable heart or haemoglobinopathy.
Stopping HCC ultrasound after cure in cirrhosis.
Giving antacids or high-dose proton pump inhibitors with velpatasvir.
keyPoints: Antibody positive is not infection: only detectable RNA or core antigen means active HCV.
Treat everyone with active infection; treatment-naive patients without cirrhosis or with CTP A cirrhosis can be treated in primary care.
Never use glecaprevir/pibrentasvir or voxilaprevir in CTP B or C cirrhosis.
Test HBsAg and anti-HBc before the first dose; stop or switch amiodarone, rifamycins, enzyme-inducing antiepileptics and St. John's wort.
Cure is HCV RNA not detected 12 weeks after treatment; surveillance for HCC continues in F3 and cirrhosis.

patientEducation: Hepatitis C can be cured with a short course of tablets taken once a day; take every dose and do not stop early.
Do not start any new medicine, herbal product or supplement without asking the treating team.
Antibodies stay positive after cure and do not protect you; you can catch the virus again.
Do not share razors, toothbrushes or needles; cover cuts; contacts and sexual partners should be tested.
Women should not become pregnant during treatment, and for 6 months after ribavirin; use two reliable methods.
lifestyleAndDiet: Avoid alcohol; it speeds liver damage even after cure.
Keep a healthy weight and control diabetes; blood sugar can fall as the virus clears, so check glucose more often.
Vaccinate against hepatitis A and hepatitis B if not immune, after treatment is finished.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician (simplified pathway); hepatologist or gastroenterologist; infectious diseases specialist (HIV, HBV coinfection); nephrologist for dialysis; liver transplant centre for decompensation; obstetrician before pregnancy; clinical pharmacist for interaction review.
dischargeCriteria: Active HCV confirmed by RNA, fibrosis stage recorded, HBV and HIV status known, interactions reviewed, regimen and duration written for the patient, SVR12 date booked, and a liver unit referral made if cirrhosis, renal impairment, prior treatment or decompensation is present.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: HCV RNA and liver tests 12 weeks after the last dose; if cured without advanced fibrosis and with normal liver tests, discharge from HCV follow-up; F3 or cirrhosis: liver ultrasound every 6 months for life, portal hypertension checks by elastography and platelets, annual HCV RNA if risk of reinfection continues; untreated or failed patients: liver tests, blood count and INR every 6 to 12 months.
